findings.evidence: "The ~199,000 row is the exception and carries [canonical scenario][DERIVED]: it consumes no illustrative input — its 9,500 tokens, its 1.08 s prefill residual, its 25 ms/token TPOT budget and its $20/hr price are all canonical (Table 4‑2)."
findings.issue: The text calls the ~199,000 row canonical, but the 9,500-token basis is derived from canonical inputs, while the 9,000/242,000/285,000 rows are marked [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]. The note is internally consistent, but the 199,000 row is the only per-dollar row using the canonical 25 ms/token basis; the table does not flag this row’s different operating point in the row itself, only in the note.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a row-level qualifier or footnote to the ~199,000 row stating that it uses the canonical 25 ms/token TPOT budget rather than the illustrative 20 ms/token rate used by the other per-dollar rows.

findings.evidence: "Per-request context/KV cost at 9.2K input — named 70B checkpoint with GQA‑8 (e.g. Llama‑2/3 70B)"
findings.issue: Table 5-2 lists "Llama‑2/3 70B" as an example of a "70B checkpoint with GQA‑8." Llama-2 70B does not use GQA (it has 64 KV-heads, standard MHA). Only Llama-3 70B uses GQA with 8 KV-heads. The slash notation "2/3" naturally reads as including both generations, so readers choosing a model from this table would wrongly assume Llama-2 70B has 8× smaller KV than the full-MHA bound. This is the same attribution error as R18-001, appearing earlier in the book.
findings.fix_instruction: Change "Llama‑2/3 70B" to "Llama‑3 70B" in Table 5-2 of Ch. 5, or to "Llama-3 70B (Llama-2 70B uses full MHA)" if the contrast is pedagogically useful.
